prompt: can you see if readme file is all upto date.

tasks.title: Audit README against current CLI behavior and workflow
tasks.spec: Review `README.md` line by line against the current implementation in the CLI and orchestration modules, especially `agentflow/cli.py`, `agentflow/config.py`, `agentflow/planner.py`, `agentflow/scheduler.py`, `agentflow/worker.py`, `agentflow/merger.py`, `agentflow/validator.py`, and `ARCHITECTURE.md`. Update the README so installation, required environment variables, supported commands, config examples, and the end-to-end workflow accurately reflect the code as it exists now. Fix any stale or incomplete descriptions, remove claims that are no longer true, add missing user-facing behaviors that are already implemented, and repair any truncated or unfinished sections in the workflow explanation. Keep the README concise and user-oriented rather than turning it into a second architecture document.
tasks.rationale: The user asked whether the README is up to date, and this is a single documentation audit centered on one primary file. Outdated onboarding docs are a user-facing defect: they cause incorrect setup, misuse of CLI commands, and wrong expectations about how planning, review, merge, retry, and validation actually work. The repo already separates high-level user docs (`README.md`) from deeper design docs (`ARCHITECTURE.md`), so the right fix is to reconcile the README with the implementation rather than splitting this into multiple tasks.
